name: org.veralabs/coach
title: VERA: AI Running Coach
description: AI that integrates wellness into your life. First up: a running coach that adapts as life happens.

tools.name: rearrange_week
tools.description: Use when a runner's training week went wrong (a missed run, less time, travel, tiredness, illness, a sore spot) and they want the rest of it adjusted. Needs the week's sessions and today's weekday; returns the VERA app's rules for changing a week and the week itself, for you to rearrange it, which check_week then checks with the app's code. Stores nothing.

week.description: The sessions of the current week, Monday to Sunday.

session.description: The session with its size, for example "Long run 18 km" or "Intervals 6 x 800 m".

status.description: Left out, days before today count as done and the rest as planned.

what_went_wrong.description: What happened to the week, in one or two sentences, only as far as it changes the training. No names, diagnoses or medication.

today.description: The weekday the runner is on.

unavailable_days.description: Days left this week with no training possible.

weeks_to_race.description: Weeks until the next race, when there is one.

language.description: The language the runner writes in. Default: guessed from their words.

tools.name: check_week
tools.description: Use when you have rearranged a week from rearrange_week, before showing it: send the same week arguments and your answer in the give_answer format. Runs the VERA app's own check (every open session placed once, nothing on a day that is over or that they cannot train) and returns either what to fix, once, or the finished week with its closing lines. Stores nothing.

week.description: The sessions of the current week, Monday to Sunday.

session.description: The session with its size, for example "Long run 18 km" or "Intervals 6 x 800 m".

status.description: Left out, days before today count as done and the rest as planned.

today.description: The weekday the runner is on.

unavailable_days.description: Days left this week with no training possible.

weeks_to_race.description: Weeks until the next race, when there is one.

language.description: The language the runner writes in. Default: guessed from their words.

round.description: 1 the first time, 2 after fixing what the first check found.

tools.name: race_paces
tools.description: Use when a runner gives a race result and asks what pace to train at or what they could run over another distance. Needs one distance and finishing time; returns predicted race times and training paces with how each should feel, and stores nothing.

distance_km.description: The race distance in km: 5 for a 5k, 10 for a 10k, 21.0975 for a half marathon, 42.195 for a marathon, 16.09 for 10 miles.

time.description: The finishing time as mm:ss or h:mm:ss, for example "49:30" or "1:52:10".

units.description: Paces per km or per mile. Default km.

tools.name: plan_to_race
tools.description: Use when someone wants a running training plan toward a race or distance (5k, 10k, half marathon, marathon, ultra), beginners included. Needs the goal, what they run in a normal week and how many days they can run; returns the VERA app's plan shape and rules for you to write the plan, which check_plan then checks with the app's code. Stores nothing.

goal_distance_km.description: The goal race distance in km: 5, 10, 21.0975 for a half marathon, 42.195 for a marathon.

weeks_to_race.description: Weeks until the race, when there is a date.

goal_time.description: The time they want to run, if they said one, for example "1:55:00".

current_weekly_km.description: What they run in a normal week now, in km. 0 for someone who does not run yet.

runs_per_week.description: How many days a week they can run.

longest_recent_run_km.description: Their longest run in the last month, in km, if they know it.

notes.description: Anything that shapes the weeks: days that do not work, other sports, a niggle, how they like to train. No names, diagnoses or medication.

language.description: The language the runner writes in. Default English.

hours_per_week.description: The hours a week they have for training, if they said. A hard limit, like their days.

age.description: Their age, if they said: easier weeks come more often from 50.

race_name.description: The race's name, if they said (a trail or mountain race is planned as trail).

tools.name: check_plan
tools.description: Use when you have written a plan from plan_to_race, before showing it: send the same runner facts and the plan you wrote, in the plan format. Runs the VERA app's own checks (weeks to race day, the runner's days and hours, every run sized) and returns either what to fix, once, or the checked plan and how to write it out. Stores nothing.

goal_distance_km.description: The goal race distance in km: 5, 10, 21.0975 for a half marathon, 42.195 for a marathon.

weeks_to_race.description: Weeks until the race, when there is a date.

language.description: The language the runner writes in. Default English.

hours_per_week.description: The hours a week they have for training, if they said. A hard limit, like their days.

age.description: Their age, if they said: easier weeks come more often from 50.

race_name.description: The race's name, if they said (a trail or mountain race is planned as trail).

long_run_day.description: The athlete's STANDING long-run weekday (0=Mon..6=Sun). Set ONLY when they state a permanent preference ('long run on Sundays — every week'); omit otherwise and any stored preference is carried forward automatically.

training_days.description: The weekdays this plan trains on, 0=Mon..6=Sun — every day with a session, runs AND any strength/cross day of its own (a session marked on_run_day takes no day), as many as the first leg's weekly_sessions. REQUIRED whenever the athlete has named their days ("Tue, Thu, Fri, Sun") or days they cannot train: use exactly those days. Omit only when they named none (an existing plan then keeps its stored days).

title.description: Short, personal title for the plan card. Use the athlete's goal or race name. Max 6 words. Examples: 'Your Berlin build', '10K race ready', 'Half marathon goal'. Never a full sentence.

start_date.description: The plan's first day, YYYY-MM-DD. Set this ONLY when the athlete is starting/re-starting and states when they began (a date, 'today', or how long they've already been training); it may be in the PAST for someone already mid-training. When you are ADJUSTING an existing plan, OMIT this — the current journey start is preserved automatically. NEVER reset it to today just because you're editing the plan. A FIRST plan built on a day you told them not to train (a cold, a niggle) starts TOMORROW, so today stays empty on the Journey instead of showing a session you just called off.

start_mode.description: 'fresh' when the athlete starts this plan from scratch this week; 'mid_training' when they're already underway and the plan back-dates into their ongoing training (pair with a past start_date).

label.description: The phase name: 'Base', 'Build', 'Sharpen' or 'Taper' (the same four for every level; a goal without a race has Base and Build). What it is for goes in description.

weekly_sessions.description: Training days a week in this leg: at most the athlete's stated days-per-week, the athlete's own days (the app holds every plan to them). Fewer is fine.

target_km.description: The leg's TOTAL km — all its weeks together, NOT per week (2 weeks of 20 km = 40).

target_elevation_m.description: Total target elevation gain in meters for this leg

target_time_min.description: Total target training time in minutes for this leg

weekly_volumes.description: Km for EACH week of this leg, one number per week (length = duration_weeks, sums to target_km). Write it for every leg you create or change — it is exactly what the athlete sees week by week.

long_run_km.description: The long run's km for EACH week of this leg, one number per week (same length as weekly_volumes), easier weeks included. Exactly what the athlete sees for the long run that week: the app adds no growth of its own. Omit for a leg without a long run.

distance_km.description: Km of ONE session of this workout — the number you told the athlete in chat (a run-walk: the km covered, e.g. 5). Runs only. REQUIRED for every run (a run-walk written in minutes may give duration_min instead). This exact number is what the athlete sees on their Journey for this session.

day.description: The weekday (0=Mon..6=Sun) this workout sits on every week, when the athlete named it or it can only go there (gym on the one day that is not a run day, intervals on the day they asked for). Must be one of training_days. Omit when any training day is fine.

duration_min.description: Minutes of ONE session of this workout (strength, mobility, cross-training; optional for runs). What the athlete sees on their Journey for this session.

on_run_day.description: Strength / mobility only: true when the athlete does it on a run day, after or before that day's run ("kettlebell after my easy run"). It then takes no training day of its own: every training day keeps its run, and it does not count toward weekly_sessions. With day set, it sits beside that day's run. Omit for a session on its own day (a gym day).

priority.description: CORE = non-negotiable session that drives the week's adaptation (typically 1-2 per week: the long run, the key quality session). FLEX = supportive volume/strength/recovery the athlete can move, shorten, or skip without derailing progress. Default to FLEX unless the session is critical.

recipe.description: What the session IS, read as it is by the Journey, the Today card, Analytics and the calendar. kind always; blocks for any session with parts (warm-up, reps of work with recovery, cool-down), exactly as you described it. 'Hill sprints 8 × 30 s, jog back down' = kind hills, block {part main, reps 8, work {sec 30}, recovery {how jog}, effort hard}.

total_km.description: The whole session's km, when you said it.

total_min.description: The whole session's minutes, when you said them.

reps.description: Repetitions of work (omit for one continuous block).

work.description: ONE repetition, or the whole block: km, m, min or sec.

recovery.description: Between repetitions: an amount and how.

description.description: What to do in this phase

plan_source.description: Set 'uploaded_static' ONLY when this plan is translated from a plan the athlete uploaded (screenshot/PDF/document) — it marks the plan as the athlete's own trusted base, which future adjustments personalize around rather than replace. Omit for plans you designed yourself.

source_note.description: With plan_source='uploaded_static': one line describing the uploaded plan (e.g. '16-week 50k plan, 4 runs/wk, screenshot upload'). Omit otherwise.

deviations.description: When the plan departs on purpose from a check you were told about (e.g. 'plan_weeks'): one entry with the check's id and your athlete-specific reason. Omit otherwise.

reason.description: Why this athlete's situation genuinely calls for the deviation

events.description: Races, competitions, or milestone events the athlete mentioned. MUST include any races the athlete talked about.

intro.description: The first message under the plan, in the runner's language, in the INTRO format.

round.description: 1 the first time, 2 after fixing what the first check found.

tools.name: plan_first_weeks
tools.description: Use when someone wants only the first two weeks of a running plan toward a goal race. Writes them from what the runner runs now: day by day, each session sized with its effort, and a short reason where it helps. Follows VERA's coaching rules: week 1 starts close to their usual week, the long run grows by a kilometre or two, most running is easy and hard sessions stay apart. Beginners get run and walk sessions. Read-only: it changes nothing in any app or calendar and needs no account. What is sent is used to write this one answer and is not stored by VERA. For running only. It is not medical advice. For a whole plan to race day, plan_to_race is the tool.

tools.name: race_day
tools.description: Use when a runner asks how to pace, fuel or prepare for a race in the last days or on race day. Needs the race distance and a goal time or recent race; returns the VERA app's race coaching and the pacing numbers, for you to write their race plan, and stores nothing.

goal_time.description: The time they hope for, mm:ss or h:mm:ss, if any.

recent_race_km.description: A recent race's distance in km, if no goal time.

climb_m.description: The race's total climbing in metres, for trail races.

race_name.description: The race's name, if they said.

notes.description: Anything that matters for this: other sports, a niggle, how they like to train. No names, diagnoses or medication.

tools.name: comeback_plan
tools.description: Use when a runner is coming back after an injury, illness or a break and asks how to restart. Needs their usual week before, the weeks off and why; returns the VERA app's comeback rules and week-by-week km, for you to write the weeks, and stores nothing.

usual_weekly_km.description: What they ran in a normal week before the break, in km.

weeks_off.description: How many weeks they ran little or nothing.

reason.description: Why they stopped: an injury, illness, or a break (holiday, work, life).

pain_now.description: True if something still hurts now.

runs_per_week.description: How many days a week they can run now.

notes.description: Anything that matters for this: other sports, a niggle, how they like to train. No names, diagnoses or medication.

language.description: The language the runner writes in. Default English.

tools.name: strength_session
tools.description: Use when a runner asks for a strength, mobility, Pilates or yoga session or routine. Takes the minutes, focus and equipment; returns the VERA app's strength and mobility rules for runners, for you to write the session, and stores nothing.

minutes.description: How long the session can be. Default 25.

focus.description: What they want. Default a mix.

equipment.description: What they have: none, a mat, dumbbells, a gym, bands.

notes.description: Anything that matters for this: other sports, a niggle, how they like to train. No names, diagnoses or medication.

language.description: The language the runner writes in. Default English.

tools.name: run_check
tools.description: Use when a runner shares one run (distance, time, maybe heart rate or km splits) and asks how it went or what it means. Returns the VERA app's run-card read against their usual and how even the splits were, for you to answer, and stores nothing.

time.description: The run's time, mm:ss or h:mm:ss.

avg_hr.description: Average heart rate, if they have it.

usual_pace.description: Their usual easy pace per km, mm:ss, if they said.

usual_hr.description: Their usual average heart rate on easy runs, if they said.

usual_km.description: How long their usual run is, in km.

splits.description: Their km splits as mm:ss, in order, if they pasted them.

felt.description: How it felt, in their words.

notes.description: Anything that matters for this: other sports, a niggle, how they like to train. No names, diagnoses or medication.

language.description: The language the runner writes in. Default English.

tools.name: training_check
tools.description: Use when a runner pastes or lists their recent runs and asks how their training is going, for a weekly recap, or if they are on track. Returns the VERA app's own Analytics read (readiness, consistency, balance), for you to write the recap, and stores nothing.

runs.description: Their sessions of the last weeks, ideally 6.

title.description: Easy run, Long run, Intervals, Strength...

race_km.description: Their goal race distance in km, if they have one.

goal_time.description: Their goal time for it, if any.

planned_weekly_km.description: The km a week their plan asks for, if they have a plan.

notes.description: Anything that matters for this: other sports, a niggle, how they like to train. No names, diagnoses or medication.

language.description: The language the runner writes in. Default English.

tools.name: hr_zones
tools.description: Use when a runner asks for heart-rate zones or what heart rate to run easy, long, tempo or intervals at. Needs their max heart rate or age; returns the VERA app's heart-rate bands per kind of session, and stores nothing.

max_hr.description: Their highest heart rate seen in a race or very hard effort, if they know it.

age.description: Their age, for an estimate when they do not know their max.

notes.description: Anything that matters for this: other sports, a niggle, how they like to train. No names, diagnoses or medication.

language.description: The language the runner writes in. Default English.

tools.name: conditions_pace
tools.description: Use when a runner asks how to adjust pace for heat, humidity, hills or altitude. Needs their normal pace and the conditions; returns how much slower the same effort runs, for you to answer, and stores nothing.

pace.description: The pace they would run in good conditions, mm:ss per km (or per mile with units mi).

distance_km.description: The run's or race's distance in km, with climb_m.

altitude_m.description: Altitude in metres above sea level.

notes.description: Anything that matters for this: other sports, a niggle, how they like to train. No names, diagnoses or medication.

language.description: The language the runner writes in. Default English.
